subject: Heliogenix dedicated sizing: tokens/sec scenarios, SLO fit, and GPU runway
messages:
From: Claire Ortiz <claire.ortiz@heliogenix.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ankit Sharma <ankit.sharma@heliogenix.io>
Date: 2027-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: initial numbers for dedicated fleet sizing

Hi Soojin — thanks for the quick chat this morning. As discussed, the internal engineering team at Heliogenix has two main workload patterns: (1) interactive assistant queries (avg 80 tokens in, 120 tokens out), ~2.5k qps at peak across EU/US users; and (2) nightly bulk document enrichment (avg 1,200 tokens total) that we run in a 6-hour window.

Key asks from procurement: a conservative tokens/sec estimate for the interactive path with p95 <= 350ms, and an estimate of committed GPU slab size (and what burst capacity looks like) so we can price the contract.

We attached a sample trace and token_profile_examples.txt from our infra team. Can you return a short table mapping token/sec -> suggested slab size (GPU SKUs) and the expected p95 under each? Also any predicted headroom numbers for a 20% growth buffer would be great.

Thanks,
Claire Ortiz
Head of Product
Heliogenix
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Ortiz <claire.ortiz@heliogenix.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-08T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: initial numbers for dedicated fleet sizing

Claire — appreciate the details. I pulled Karthik in to run the throughput modeling and Marissa for the SLA/contract implications. High level first pass below; we'll follow up with the spreadsheet.

Summary (interactive assistant):
- Avg token per request (roundtrip): 200 tokens
- Target SLO: p95 latency <= 350ms end-to-end (inference only target p95 <= 280ms to allow network/client adders)
- Baseline model candidate: redwood-llama-13b-quant (serving profile we validated last quarter)

Rough throughput-to-slab mapping (conservative):
- 40k tokens/sec -> 2x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (sustained), p95 ~ 220–270ms
- 80k tokens/sec -> 4x A100-80GB equiv, p95 ~ 240–320ms (tail depends on concurrency and KV cache hit rate)
- 120k tokens/sec -> 6x A100-80GB equiv, p95 ~ 310–380ms (edge of SLO if cold starts/cold KV)

Nightly batch (enrichment):
- 1,200 tokens/request * 300k requests -> ~360M tokens over 6 hours (~16.7k tokens/sec sustained during window)
- This can be absorbed by the same slab if scheduled into quiet hours; guidance below on shaping.

Next steps: Karthik will paste the more detailed per-variant math and assumptions into the attached spreadsheet and call out where quantization or KV caching changes the slab sizing. Marissa will propose contract language for burst and headroom.

Best,
Soojín Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Ortiz <claire.ortiz@heliogenix.io>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-08T14:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: initial numbers for dedicated fleet sizing

Claire / team — I expanded the numbers in the attached heliogenix_capacity_scenarios.xlsx and included the micro assumptions here so you can sanity-check:

Assumptions (inference runtime):
- Model: redwood-llama-13b-quant, token compute cost: 0.00013 GPU-seconds/token on our optimized kernel (measured at seq_len 256 typical)
- Single A100-80GB equiv sustained token throughput: ~20k tokens/sec (conservative for mixed request sizes with KV cache warm), peaking to ~26k with contiguous batching for similar-sized requests
- p95 latency projection derived from combined per-token compute and batching delay model: p95_latency_ms = compute_ms + batching_wait_ms + kv_miss_penalty_ms

Detailed scenario math (short):
- For 40k tokens/sec target: tokens_per_gpu = 20k -> need 2 GPUs. compute_ms (per request average) ~ 140ms, batching_wait ~ 50–80ms depending on concurrency, KV miss penalty 10–20ms -> p95 ~ 200–240ms.
- For 80k tokens/sec: 4 GPUs, compute_ms ~ 160ms (slight scheduler pressure), batching_wait ~ 80–120ms -> p95 ~ 240–320ms.
- For 120k tokens/sec: 6 GPUs, compute_ms ~ 190ms, batching_wait ~ 120–170ms, KV miss risk increases -> p95 ~ 310–380ms (this is why 120k is near SLO boundary).

Headroom / growth buffer guidance:
- Recommend committed slab = scenario for 80k tokens/sec (4 GPUs) if you expect moderate growth.
- Include a 25% burst pool (on-demand GPUs) for sudden spikes in qps or model fallback (Doc: burst policy).
- If you need a firm p95 <= 280ms under 20% growth, upgrade to 5x A100-equivalent with autoscaling thresholds tuned at 70% sustained token utilization.

Operational notes:
- KV caching reduces per-request compute by up to 22% for common prefixes; we recommend a user-level cache TTL tuned to your interactive pattern.
- Nightly bulk: shift to lower-priority lanes that accept longer latency; this reduces interactive slab needs.

I added the per-minute token contour heatmap (sheet: contour) and a sample autoscaler policy (sheet: autoscale).

-Karthik
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Ortiz <claire.ortiz@heliogenix.io>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-09T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: initial numbers for dedicated fleet sizing

Claire — looping in commercial items and SLA language so procurement has something to work from. Two quick contract-relevant bullets:

1) Commitment recommendation (commercial):
- Base commitment: 4x A100-80GB equiv reserved (covers ~80k tokens/sec sustained)
- Burst allowance: up to 25% above committed for up to 10 minutes per hour (metered and billable at burst rate unless an uplift is contracted)
- Optional 12-month growth clause: a one-time true-up cap that allows +1 GPU in the reserved slab at a pre-agreed price if average sustained token/sec increases by >20% for 30 consecutive days.

2) SLA & SLO framing:
- Platform SLO: p95 inference latency <= 350ms measured at service edge.
- Performance objective for the dedicated slab in contract: p95 inference latency <= 280ms for 95% of months, measured across production traffic, with clear remediation steps if violated (investigation window, mitigation credits capped at X% of monthly fee).
- We will include required instrumentation (traces, token-level latency breakdown) as part of onboarding so both sides can validate headroom assumptions.

Attachments: I attached a redlined SLA (Heliogenix_SLA_draft_v2.pdf) with the remediation timeline and suggested credit tiers.

If that looks ok, Soojin / Claire — propose a 30-minute procurement sync tomorrow to walk the spreadsheet and confirm the commit level.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Manager, Sales Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference
